subject: math
title: Grade 8 Percents: Over 100%, Under 1%, Percent Change and HST
seo_title: Grade 8 Percents Worksheets: Over 100%, Under 1% and Percent Change, Free Math with Answer Key (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Use fractions, decimal numbers, and percents, including percents of more than 100% or less than 1%, interchangeably and flexibly to solve a variety of problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 math worksheets on percents for the Ontario curriculum: percents over 100% and under 1%, converting fractions, decimals and percents, percent increase and decrease, and HST, discount and population growth problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: 150% = 1.5 and 0.5% = 0.005.
body_html:
Percent means “out of 100”

To use a percent in a calculation, divide it by 100 to get a decimal. Then multiply. This works for every percent: 25%, 150% or 0.5%.

PercentDecimalFractionSize compared with the whole
150%1.5112more than the whole
100%11the whole
12.5%0.12518less than the whole
1%0.011100one hundredth
0.5%0.0051200half of one hundredth

Percents over 100%

100% is the whole amount. A percent over 100% gives more than the amount you started with.

Example

What is 150% of 40?

150% = 1.5. 1.5 × 40 = 60.

Answer: 60

Percents under 1%

A percent under 1% is a very small part. Find 1% first (divide by 100), then take part of it.

Example

What is 0.5% of 2000?

1% of 2000 = 20. 0.5% is half of 1%: 20 ÷ 2 = 10.

Answer: 10

Percent increase and decrease

Percent change = change ÷ starting value × 100. To increase by 20%, multiply by 1.2. To decrease by 15%, multiply by 0.85.

Percent change

A price rises from $20 to $25. What is the percent increase?

Change = $5. Divide by the starting price: 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25.

Answer: 25%

HST

A $40 hoodie plus 13% HST. What is the total?

13% of $40 = 0.13 × 40 = $5.20. $40 + $5.20 = $45.20. Or 1.13 × $40 = $45.20.

Answer: $45.20

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
150% of 40 = 40 + 150 = 190150% = 1.5, so 1.5 × 40 = 60
0.5% = 0.5 (one half)0.5% = 0.5 ÷ 100 = 0.005
0.5% of 2000 = 10001% of 2000 is 20, so 0.5% is 10
$20 to $25 is a 5% increaseDivide the change by the start: 5 ÷ 20 = 25%
Increase 60 by 150% = 9090 is 150% of 60. Add it on: 60 + 90 = 150

faq.q: What do Grade 8 students learn about percents in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 8 math curriculum, students use fractions, decimals and percents interchangeably, including percents of more than 100% and less than 1%, to solve problems such as percent increase and decrease, sales tax and discounts.

faq.q: How do you find a percent of a number that is more than 100%?
faq.a: Write the percent as a decimal and multiply. For 150% of 40, 150% = 1.5 and 1.5 × 40 = 60, which is more than 40 because 150% is more than the whole.

faq.q: How do you find a percent that is less than 1%?
faq.a: Find 1% first by dividing by 100, then take part of it. For 0.5% of 2000, 1% is 20 and 0.5% is half of that, so the answer is 10.

faq.q: How do you calculate percent increase or decrease?
faq.a: Subtract to find the change, divide it by the starting value, then multiply by 100. From $20 to $25 the change is $5, and 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25, so the increase is 25%.

sets.title: Percents over 100%: 150%, 200% and 350% of a number

items.e: 200% = 2, so 200% of 35 = 2 × 35 = 70. 235 adds 200 to 35, and 17.5 halves 35 instead of doubling it.
125% = 1.25. 100% of 80 is 80 and 25% is 20, so 80 + 20 = 100. 205 adds 125 to 80, 20 is only the extra 25%, and 1000 uses 12.5 instead of 1.25.
Percent means out of 100, so 125% = 125 ÷ 100 = 1.25. The calculation is 1.25 × 64 (= 80). 12.5 and 0.125 move the decimal point the wrong number of places, and 64 + 125 adds the percent.

items.q: Without calculating, which amount is greater than 72?
items.e: 100% of 72 is 72 itself. A percent over 100% gives more than the number, so 125% of 72 is greater than 72. 75% and 99% give less than 72, and 100% gives exactly 72.

items.q: The double number line shows that 100% is 64. What amount matches 150%?
items.e: On the line, 100% matches 64, so 50% matches 32. 150% = 100% + 50%: 64 + 32 = 96. 214 adds 150 to 64, 32 is only 50%, and 128 is 200%.
1812 = 1.5 = 150%. 18 is more than 12, so the answer must be more than 100%. 50% is only the extra 6, 1.5% forgets to multiply by 100, and 6% uses the difference.
4520 = 2.25 = 225%. Check: 225% of 20 = 2.25 × 20 = 45. 125% is only the extra 25, 2.25% forgets to multiply by 100, and 25% uses the difference 45 − 20.

items.q: Which is greater: 150% of 30 or 30% of 150?
items.e: 150% of 30 = 1.5 × 30 = 45. 30% of 150 = 0.3 × 150 = 45. They are equal: a% of b is always the same as b% of a.

items.q: 150% of a number is 60. What is the number?
items.e: 1.5 × ? = 60, so ? = 60 ÷ 1.5 = 40. Check: 150% of 40 = 60. 90 is 150% of 60 (the wrong way round), 30 halves 60, and 400 divides by 0.15.

items.q: 200% of a number is 52. What is the number?
items.e: 200% = 2, so 2 × ? = 52 and ? = 52 ÷ 2 = 26. 104 is 200% of 52 (the wrong way round), 13 divides by 4, and 260 divides by 0.2.

sets.title: Percents under 1%: 0.5%, 0.25% and 0.1% of a number

items.e: 1% of 800 is 8, so 0.5% is half of 8 = 4. 400 treats 0.5% as one half, and 40 is 5%.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: One whole square is 1% of the grid. Only half of one square is shaded, so the shaded part is 0.5%: less than 1%. 50% would be half of the whole grid.
1% of 1200 is 12. 0.75% is three quarters of 1%: 12 ÷ 4 × 3 = 9. 900 is 75%, and 90 is 7.5%.
31000 = 0.003. Multiply by 100: 0.3%. 3% would be 30 out of 1000.
1400 = 0.0025 = 0.25%. Check: 1% of 400 is 4, so 1 is a quarter of 1%. 25% of 400 would be 100.
1% of 500 = 5. 0.8% of 500 = 4, which is less, so 0.8% of 500. 1.2% of 500 = 6, and 10% of 50 and 5% of 100 are both exactly 5.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: Compare the decimals: 0.09 < 0.50 < 1. So 0.09%, 0.5%, 1%. 0.09% has the digit 9, but it is less than one tenth of 1%.
1% of 36 is 0.36. 0.5% is half of that: 0.18. 18 treats 0.5% as one half, 1.8 is 5%, and 0.018 is 0.05%.

items.q: 0.5% of a number is 6. What is the number?
items.e: 0.5% = 0.005, so ? = 6 ÷ 0.005 = 1200. Or: 0.5% is 6, so 1% is 12 and 100% is 1200. 12 divides by 0.5, and 3 takes half of 6.
Percent means out of 100, so divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.5% = 0.005. 0.5 forgets to divide, and 0.05 moves only one place.
Divide by 100: 150% = 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5. 150% is more than 100%, so the decimal is more than 1.
Multiply by 100: move the decimal point 2 places right. 0.07 = 7%. 70% would be 0.7.
Multiply by 100: 2.4 × 100 = 240%. 2.4 is more than 1, so the percent is more than 100%. 24% moves the decimal point only one place.
Multiply by 100: 0.003 × 100 = 0.3%. The number is less than 0.01, so the percent is less than 1%.
1.05 × 100 = 105%. 10.5% moves the decimal point only one place, and 15% drops the zero.
Divide by 100: move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.65% = 0.0065. 0.65 forgets to divide, and 0.065 moves only one place.
0.4% = 0.4 ÷ 100 = 0.004 = 41000 = 1250. 0.04 is 4%, 0.4 is 40%, and 4 is 400%.

items.q: Write 18 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 = 12.5%. 8% uses the denominator, and 18% just joins the digits of 18.

items.q: Write 38 as a percent.
items.e: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Multiply by 100: 37.5%. 3.8% reads 38 as 3.8, 0.375% forgets to multiply by 100, and 62.5% is 58.

items.q: Write 54 as a percent.
items.e: 5 ÷ 4 = 1.25 = 125%. The fraction is more than 1, so the percent is more than 100%. 80% is 45 (the fraction flipped).

items.q: Write 1200 as a percent.
items.e: 1 ÷ 200 = 0.005. Multiply by 100: 0.5%. Check: 1% is 1100, and 1200 is half of that. 0.005% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: Which is equal to 11000?
items.e: 11000 = 0.001. Multiply by 100: 0.1%. 1% is 1100.

items.q: Write 0.2% as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.2% = 0.2100 = 21000 = 1500. 15 is 20%, and 150 is 2%.
250% = 250100 = 2.5 = 212. 25 reads 2.5 as “2 over 5”, 215 reads 0.5 as one fifth, and 25 divides by 10 instead of 100.

items.q: Write 234 as a percent.
items.e: 234 = 2.75. Multiply by 100: 275%. 75% forgets the 2 wholes, and 2.75% forgets to multiply by 100.
Write both as decimals. 0.8% = 0.008. 0.08 > 0.008, so 0.08 is greater (0.08 = 8%).
150% = 1.5, 32 = 1.5 and 112 = 1.5. 15% = 0.15, so it is not equal to 1.5.
Write all as decimals: 1.3, 125% = 1.25, 65 = 1.2, 0.9% = 0.009. The greatest is 1.3. 125 looks big, but 125% is only 1.25.

items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
items.e: Write all as decimals: 98% = 0.98, 98 = 1.125, 1.2. So the order is 98%, 98, 1.2.
25% of 40 = 10. Increase: 40 + 10 = 50. Or 125% of 40 = 1.25 × 40 = 50. 65 adds 25, 10 is only the increase, and 30 is a decrease.
15% of 80 = 8 + 4 = 12. Decrease: 80 − 12 = 68. Or 85% of 80 = 68. 65 subtracts 15, 12 is only the decrease, and 92 is an increase.
40% of 45 = 18. 45 − 18 = 27. Or 60% of 45 = 27. 5 subtracts 40, and 18 is only the decrease.

items.q: A value changes from 20 to 25. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 25 − 20 = 5. Divide by the starting value: 520 = 0.25 = 25%. 5% uses the change as a percent, 20% divides by the new value (525), and 125% is 25 as a percent of 20.

items.q: A value changes from 50 to 40. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 50 − 40 = 10. Divide by the starting value: 1050 = 20%. 25% divides by the new value (1040), and 80% is 40 as a percent of 50.
12.5% = 18, so 12.5% of 64 = 8. 64 + 8 = 72. 76.5 adds 12.5, and 56 is a decrease.

items.q: A value changes from 16 to 4. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Change = 16 − 4 = 12. 1216 = 0.75 = 75%. 300% divides by the new value (124), and 25% is 4 as a percent of 16.

items.q: Multiplying a number by 1.2 is the same as which change?
items.e: 1.2 = 120% = 100% + 20%. You keep the whole number and add 20%: a 20% increase. A 120% increase would multiply by 2.2.

items.q: Multiplying a number by 0.85 is the same as which change?
items.e: 0.85 = 85% = 100% − 15%. You keep 85% and lose 15%: a 15% decrease. An 85% decrease would leave only 15%.

items.q: A price doubles. What is the percent increase?
items.e: The new price is 200% of the old price. The increase is 200% − 100% = 100%. 200% is the new price as a percent of the old one.

items.q: A value changes from 30 to 75. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 75 − 30 = 45. 4530 = 1.5 = 150%. 250% is 75 as a percent of 30 (the new value is 250% of the old one), 45% uses the change, and 60% divides by the new value (4575).

items.q: A value changes from 8 to 24. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 24 − 8 = 16. 168 = 2 = 200%. 24 is three times 8 (300% of 8), but the increase is 2 times 8.
0.5% of 200 = 1. 200 − 1 = 199. 100 treats 0.5% as one half, 190 takes off 5%, and 199.5 subtracts 0.5.

items.q: A value changes from 2000 to 2010. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 10. 102000 = 0.005 = 0.5%. 10% uses the change as a percent, and 5% and 0.05% move the decimal point the wrong number of places.

items.q: A value changes from 250 to 300. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Change = 50. 50250 = 0.2 = 20%. 50% uses the change, 120% is 300 as a percent of 250, and 0.2% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: Increase 100 by 10%. Then decrease the result by 10%. What is the final value?
items.e: 100 + 10 = 110. 10% of 110 = 11, so 110 − 11 = 99. The second 10% is of 110, not 100, so the changes do not cancel out.

items.q: After a 20% increase, a number is 60. What was the number before the increase?
items.e: After the increase the number is 120% of the start: 1.2 × ? = 60, so ? = 60 ÷ 1.2 = 50. Check: 20% of 50 = 10, and 50 + 10 = 60. 48 takes 20% of 60 away, but the 20% is of the starting number.

items.q: After a 25% decrease, a number is 60. What was the number before the decrease?
items.e: After the decrease the number is 75% of the start: 0.75 × ? = 60, so ? = 60 ÷ 0.75 = 80. Check: 25% of 80 = 20, and 80 − 20 = 60. 75 adds 25% of 60, and 85 adds 25.

sets.title: Word problems: HST, discounts and population growth

items.q: Noah buys a $40 hoodie. Ontario HST is 13%. What is the total with tax?
Skates that cost $120 are 30% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 30% of $120 = $36. $120 − $36 = $84. $90 takes away 30 dollars, $36 is the discount, and $156 adds the discount.

items.q: A savings account pays 0.5% interest a month. Leah has $1600 in it. How much interest does she earn in one month?
items.e: 1% of $1600 = $16, so 0.5% is half: $8. $800 treats 0.5% as one half, $80 is 5%, and 80¢ is 0.05%.

items.q: A school has 750 students. On one day, 0.4% of them are absent. How many students are absent?
A hockey league has 150% as many players this year as last year. Last year it had 240 players. How many players does it have this year?
items.e: “150% as many” means 150% of 240: 1.5 × 240 = 360. 390 adds 150, 600 is an increase by 150%, and 120 is only 50%.

items.q: A town has 12 000 people. The population grows by 5%. What is the new population?
items.e: 5% of 12 000 = 600. 12 000 + 600 = 12 600. 12 005 adds 5 people, 600 is only the growth, and 13 200 grows by 10%.

items.q: The CN Tower is 553 m tall. A model of it is 0.1% of the real height. How tall is the model?
Winter boots that cost $80 are on sale for $68. What percent is the discount?
items.e: Discount = $80 − $68 = $12. 1280 = 0.15 = 15%. 12% uses the $12 as a percent, 85% is the part you pay, and 1.5% moves the decimal point only one place.

items.q: Last winter, 120 cm of snow fell in a town. This winter, 90 cm fell. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 120 − 90 = 30 cm. 30120 = 0.25 = 25%. 30% uses the 30 cm as a percent, 75% is this winter as a percent of last winter, and 0.25% forgets to multiply by 100.

items.q: A town grew from 8000 to 10 000 people. What is the percent increase?
items.e: Increase = 2000. Divide by the starting population: 20008000 = 25%. 20% divides by the new population, 2000% uses the increase, and 125% is the new population as a percent of the old one.

items.q: In a survey, 0.6 of the students chose hockey and 14 chose soccer. The rest chose basketball. What percent chose basketball?
items.e: 0.6 = 60% and 14 = 25%. 100% − 60% − 25% = 15%. 85% is hockey and soccer together, and 40% forgets to take away soccer. 75% takes away only soccer.

items.q: A town of 40 000 people holds a Terry Fox Run. 0.25% of the people volunteer. How many volunteers is that?
A phone plan includes 5 GB of data. Ethan uses 6.5 GB. What percent of the plan did he use?
items.e: 6.55 = 1.3 = 130%. He used more than the plan, so the answer is more than 100%. 30% is only the extra, and 65% divides by 10.

items.q: Kai buys a used bike for $150 and sells it for $180. What is the percent increase in price?
items.e: Increase = $30. 30150 = 0.2 = 20%. 30% uses the $30 as a percent, and 120% is $180 as a percent of $150.

items.q: A town’s population fell from 25 000 to 24 500. What is the percent decrease?
items.e: Decrease = 500. 50025 000 = 0.02 = 2%. 5%, 20% and 0.2% put the decimal point in the wrong place.

items.q: A town of 10 000 people grows by 10% each year for 2 years. What is the population after 2 years?
items.e: After 1 year: 10% of 10 000 = 1000, so 11 000. After 2 years: 10% of 11 000 = 1100, so 11 000 + 1100 = 12 100. 12 000 adds 10% of 10 000 twice, but the second 10% is of the bigger number. 11 000 is only one year, and 10 020 adds just 10 people a year.

items.q: A jacket costs $60. It is 25% off, and then 13% HST is added to the sale price. What is the total?
items.e: 25% of $60 = $15, so the sale price is $45. 13% of $45 = $5.85. $45 + $5.85 = $50.85. $67.80 forgets the discount, $45 forgets the tax, and $52.80 takes off 25% − 13% = 12%.

items.q: A meal costs $50 before tax. HST is 13%, and the family leaves a 15% tip on the price before tax. What is the total?
items.e: HST: 13% of $50 = $6.50. Tip: 15% of $50 = $7.50. $50 + $6.50 + $7.50 = $64. $78 adds 13 and 15 dollars, and $57.50 and $56.50 each forget one of the two parts.

items.q: Emma pays $34 for a sweater that is 15% off. What was the price before the sale?
items.e: She pays 100% − 15% = 85% of the price. 0.85 × ? = $34, so ? = $34 ÷ 0.85 = $40. Check: 15% of $40 = $6, and $40 − $6 = $34. $39.10 adds 15% of $34, but the 15% is of the original price. $49 adds 15 dollars, and $28.90 takes 15% off again.

items.q: A board game costs $56.50 including 13% HST. What was the price before tax?
items.e: The total is 113% of the price: 1.13 × ? = $56.50, so ? = $56.50 ÷ 1.13 = $50. Check: 13% of $50 = $6.50. $43.50 subtracts 13 dollars, $63 adds the $6.50 tax a second time, and $6.50 is only the tax.
